item.title: Point Equivalence, Lie Symmetries, and Laurent Compatibility of the Time-Dependent Modified Dispersive Water-Wave System
item.description: arXiv:2611.33199v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify local point transformations between members of the \((2+1)\)-dimensional modified dispersive water-wave class with two nowhere-zero real-analytic time-dependent coefficients. A change of time reduces the class to a single coefficient \(q\). An invertible differential substitution identifies this class with a slice of a previously classified coupled system and supplies a family of point maps. A direct calculation in the original field variables proves that the induced coefficient action \(\widetilde q(F(T))=q(T)/k\), with \(F'>0\) and \(k\ne0\) constant, exhausts all local point identifications. The order and relative sign of the first nonzero derivative classify nonconstant pointed coefficient germs. Constant germs admit arbitrary time generators, regular nonconstant germs admit one independent time generator modulo the zero-time-component subalgebra, and critical nonconstant germs admit none through the base time. On movable analytic hypersurfaces with \(\phi_x\phi_y\ne0\), the double-pole and regular-\(V\) Laurent branches both have an obstruction at resonance \(j=2\) proportional to \(q'\). Both branches are formally compatible exactly for constant \(q\), which is also the precise criterion for point equivalence to the standard system.
item.dc:creator: Manjit Singh

item.title: Orbital Stability of Smooth Traveling Solitary Waves to the Fornberg-Whitham Equation
item.description: arXiv:2605.19906v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Fornberg-Whitham (FW) equation was introduced by Fornberg and Whitham [Fornberg and Whitham, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. A (1978)] as a nonlocal model for unidirectional shallow water waves capable of capturing wave steepening and breaking. Despite its similarities with integrable shallow-water equations, the FW equation is not completely integrable. Nevertheless, the FW equation is part of the family of peakon-type models as it supports peaked traveling wave solutions. In this paper, we consider smooth solitary wave solutions to the FW equation. We use a variational approach to show that some are orbitally stable.
item.dc:creator: Xijun Deng, Stephane Lafortune, Zhisu Liu
